Description:
Make the AMS Booth Your Base at the 107th Annual Meeting

Need a place to rest or connect? Want to explore the exhibit hall, get an Annual Meeting pin, or learn more about AMS? The AMS Booth has you covered!

At the booth, located in the 107th Annual Meeting Exhibit Hall, you’ll find spaces to work or relax, plus all the latest information about the conference and AMS. We also offer the chance to meet AMS leaders throughout the week and share your thoughts and ideas. Stop by for cupcakes during the Opening Reception on Monday, 11 January. 

Meet AMS Leaders

We anticipate that the AMS President-elect, President, and two past Presidents will visit the booth on Wednesday, 13 January from 10:00 to 10:45 a.m. to connect with you, discuss their work, and chat about AMS initiatives. Please stop by to share your thoughts on what’s working, what’s not, and what you would like to see next. AMS leaders also welcome your thoughts on how the reductions to the Federal workforce and drastic cuts to research funding are impacting you, and how you think AMS should respond to evolving challenges and opportunities in the field.

Get Career Guidance

Visit the AMS Career Advising Center for general career guidance, resume reviews, mock interviews, LinkedIn profile tips, and AMS certification options on Monday, 11 January from 6:00-7:30 p.m., Tuesday, 12 January from 3:00-4:30 p.m. and Wednesday 13 January from 3:00-4:30 p.m.

Help Shape AMS Climate Training Materials

Visit the AMS Career Advising Center to test-drive a prototype online lesson, Climate Science Fundamentals, alongside AMS and COMET staff. The lesson supports the AMS Certificate in Climate Science, designed to equip practitioners with core climate knowledge and practical applications.

Feedback is especially needed from students, early-career scientists, and meteorology or Earth science professionals without formal education in climate and climate variability.

Demo Sessions:

  • Monday, Jan 11: 6:00–7:30 p.m.

  • Tuesday, Jan 12: 3:00–4:30 p.m.

  • Wednesday, Jan 13: 3:00–4:30 p.m.

Work, Relax, and Connect

The AMS Booth features high-top workstation where you can plug in and get things done, or cozy coffee tables where you can unplug and have casual conversations with fellow attendees.

Learn More About AMS

Want to learn more about AMS member benefits and resources, community engagement opportunities, certification programs, the AMS Policy Program, K-12 education, or early career support? Our booth staff will have everything you need to get involved and stay informed about AMS and all that’s available to our members. 

Other Booth Highlights: 

  • Check out images from past AMS photo contest finalists and highlights from across AMS meetings and programs.
  • Pick up an AMS Journals bookmark.
  • A limited number of Annual Meeting pins are available – come early in the week to make sure you get one! 
  • Join the AMS Connections Lounges that will be taking place in the booth.

We can’t wait to see you at the AMS Booth. Come by, say hi, and get to know your home base for all things AMS at the 107th Annual Meeting!

Description:
At Baron Weather, we understand how difficult it can be to integrate and use weather data and technology in a way that benefits your organization. Whether you’re a part of a government, commercial, or media enterprise, we believe you deserve to be optimally equipped to make informed decisions that protect your assets, improve safety and efficiencies, and increase revenue. That’s why Baron provides best-in-class, superior weather intelligence with meteorological tools that set the industry standard for radar engineering, hydrological modeling, data integration, and severe weather monitoring.

In fact, throughout our rich history of relentless innovation, we have developed a wide range of products and weather data that offers effective solutions for the prediction, tracking, analysis, and mitigation of meteorological events. This means Baron offers accurate tools, comprehensive weather data, and solutions that enable our customers to communicate the impact of weather.

Baron’s Gen-3 radar series is the ultimate differentiator, providing state-of-the-art technology, processing, and calibration. And we continue to invest in dual-polarization radar research and development to optimize the hardware, interpret the data, and develop value-added data products.

Working in tandem with Baron’s dual-pol radars, our new radar clutter mitigation technology, ClearScan, provides a clear depiction of actual precipitation. Using machine learning algorithms supported by human intervention, Baron’s ClearScan learns to recognize data from actual weather targets versus radio frequency interference caused by electronic devices. As new technologies like 5G cellular signals increase the potential interference with weather radars, this capability has grown to be of the utmost importance.

Baron maintains it place at the forefront of meteorological science by continuously cultivating new modeling techniques for issues such as air quality and flooding. Our forecast modeling also demonstrates weather conditions like precipitation, wind, and winter weather with robust accuracy.

Our wide range of scientific applications are available to customers domestically as well as abroad for integration into existing networks and infrastructures.

We ensure you’re treated as a partner, not a date point. Plus, Baron customers enjoy unrivaled 24/7 customer support from degreed meteorologists.

Description:
Originally developed in 1985 by the Norwegian Geotechnical Institute (NGI) & Geonor to provide accurate snow accumulation measurements for avalanche predictions, the T-200B Series Precipitation Gauges are now used around the world to accurately measure precipitation of all types. Several thousand gauges have been delivered and installed in locations ranging from very remote sites to dense urban areas. They are used to measure a variety of hydrological applications from flood forecasting and agricultural monitoring, to watershed catchment and snow-pack run-off prediction.

The T-200B Series now include several different capacity gauges from 600-mm (24-inches) up to 3000-mm (120-inches). Along with the inner & outer Alter windscreens, pedestals, and an optional heater, the T-200B Series provides unsurpassed measurement of precipitation rates for flood prediction as well as total accumulation. With a minimal temperature drift (0.001% FS /°C) and proven reliability, 1 the T-200B Series Precipitation Gauges continue to demonstrate their reliability, durability, and precision across diverse environments.

1 - The WMO 2007 Workshop Summary: Ensuring Quality Long-Term Monitoring With Precipitation Gauges, Dr. Elizabeth Weatherhead.
With more than 100 Geonor T-200B gauges, The Swedish Meteorological & Hydrological Institute (SMHI) observed only five sensors break in seven years (7,052,000 network hours) of operation, (Ann-Christine Andersson and Sverker Hellström of SMHI).

Description:
REMTECH is a company with offices in France and the U.S.A. which manufactures and maintains the REMTECH DOPPLER SODAR(s) and the RASS (Radio Acoustic Sounding System).

Our DOPPLER SODAR systems measure remotely a vertical profile of wind speed, direction, thermal stratification and turbulence parameters (sigma W, sigma Theta) up to 400, 700, and 3,000 meters average altitude range depending on Sodar model.

They are ideally suited for wind energy site assessment, airport safety (wind shear detection), for air pollution control and forecast, site surveys (power plants).

Military organizations are using the SODAR in programs for weapons development, parachuting, landing on aircraft carriers as well as flight tests in general.

Our RASS remotely measures temperature profiles in the atmosphere. It can be used in environmental studies and study of telecommunication network disturbances due to atmospheric conditions. It comes as an option to our long range SODAR and can provide measurements up to 1,500 meters above ground.

REMTECH has sold more than 700 SODAR’s and 50 RASS systems in 65 countries.

Description:
PlanetiQ is a leading commercial provider of high-quality GNSS radio occultation (GNSS-RO) data for weather forecasting, atmospheric research, and space weather applications. Through its proprietary constellation of satellites and advanced measurement technology, PlanetiQ delivers the highest-precision GNSS-RO measurements available, with exceptional signal quality and temporal, spatial, and vertical resolution.

PlanetiQ data is used in operational Numerical Weather Prediction (NWP) models and next-generation AI forecasting systems to improve atmospheric analysis and forecast accuracy. Its high-resolution measurements provide valuable information throughout the atmosphere, including in regions where conventional observing systems have limited coverage. PlanetiQ also provides ionospheric measurements that support space weather monitoring and research, as well as dual-polarization observations that offer new insights into precipitation.

PlanetiQ is a major supplier of commercial satellite data to the U.S. government, including NOAA and NASA. In 2025, the company received NOAA's largest-ever contract for commercial satellite weather data. PlanetiQ has since secured a multi-year task order for GNSS-RO under NOAA NESDIS's Satellite-Based Earth and Model Environmental Monitoring (SBEM) program.
Title: PlanetiQ

Description:
For many years, the Exosens team has been working to help environmental industries and researchers address increasingly complex monitoring and measurement challenges. The ASSIST-II is a field deployable sounder which uses Fourier Transform technology. It is the latest development in ground-based atmospheric sounding spectrometer. Its configuration is rugged, compact and can be adapted to various environments, such as snowy regions and sea platforms. Thanks to its advanced software suite, it can be operated 24/7 to provide atmospheric profiles of various components at high temporal and spectral resolutions as well as a wide choice of other applications.

Since 2000, Exosens' Québec City team has been a recognized specialist in infrared imaging and hyperspectral sensing technologies. We design and manufacture high-performance systems for a wide range of industrial and academic research applications. In addition, we offer R&D services in optical system development, tailored to meet the specific needs of our customers. Whether you require advanced thermal imaging solutions or custom optical technologies, our team provides the expertise and innovation needed to meet your exacting requirements.

With an extensive international sales network, Exosens serves customers worldwide, delivering high-end products and solutions across multiple industries. The company places strong emphasis on collaboration, responsiveness and customer satisfaction, working closely with its partners to develop solutions tailored to their specific needs.

Experience the excellence of Exosens and discover how its advanced technologies can support your most demanding applications.

Description:
Earthmover is the cloud-native platform for weather, climate, and geospatial data. Built by the maintainers of the popular open-source Xarray, Zarr, and Icechunk packages, Earthmover’s data model based on tensors (rather than tables) is the natural fit for weather forecasts, climate models, and hyperspectral Earth-observation data. With cloud-optimized tensor storage, advanced data catalog and governance, high-performance data loaders, and geospatial API integrations, Earthmover supports customers in research, energy, insurance and finance to develop and operationalize state-of-the-art AI models for prediction and decision making.

With the launch of the Earthmover Data Marketplace in early 2026, Earthmover became the market-leading provider of AI ready weather data. Earthmover data sources include highly referenced data sets from government entities like ECMWF and NOAA, including IFS initial conditions, GFS, ERA5 and HRRR. Earthmover Data Marketplace providers include industry innovators such as Brightband, Planette, Beyond Weather, Zeus AI, The Climate Uncertainty Lab, Dynamical.org, and the Sub-Seasonal Consortium.

Description:
The Institute of Atmospheric Physics (IAP), Chinese Academy of Sciences, presents three international journals: Advances in Atmospheric Sciences (AAS), Atmospheric and Oceanic Science Letters (AOSL), and EarthSphere.

AAS is dedicated to publishing original, cutting-edge research in atmospheric dynamics, physics, and chemistry, and in coupled Earth-system processes involving the atmosphere. The journal aims to advance atmospheric science, serve the global scientific community in atmospheric science and related fields, and support the achievement of sustainable development goals.

AOSL is an Open Access journal for the fast publication of original communications-length articles related to all aspects of the atmospheric sciences, oceanography, and closely related sciences. Limited manuscript size expedites the review and publication process.

EarthSphere is dedicated to the study of global change through the lens of Earth system interactions. We publish high-impact research on coupled processes among the atmosphere, oceans, cryosphere, land, solid Earth, ecosystems, and human societies. Bridging natural sciences, engineering, and solutions, our mission is to advance scientific understanding and deliver actionable pathways toward a sustainable planet.
Title: Institute of Atmospheric Physics, Chinese Academy of Sciences

Description:
WindBorne Systems has developed WindBorne Atlas, a continuous and growing constellation of hundreds of long-duration "Global Sounding Balloons" (GSB). Each balloon in the constellation can repeatedly ascend and descend to collect vertical profiles from 1 - 20km above the surface. Each GSB can

  • Stay aloft for several weeks and travel thousands of miles, even circumnavigating the globe.
  • Collect 40-50 vertical profiles of the atmosphere in a single flight.
  • Be launched and directed anywhere, targeting specific regions, countries, emerging storms, and other phenomena in even the most remote places on earth.

By January of 2027, WindBorne Atlas will consist of nearly 1000 balloon and will provide observations throughout the world. Data from Atlas provides an unprecedented level of global data that is being used for initialization to provide the most accurate weather forecasts. WindBorne Atlas is being used by NOAA, the U.S. Air Force, the U.S. Navy, and more.

WindBorne will also demonstrate the capabilities of WindBorne WeatherMesh, our AI-based weather forecasting model that is driven by WindBorne Atlas. WeatherMesh is currently the most accurate AI-based model in the world, outperforming both traditional physics-based models and other AI models in medium-range predictions. WeatherMesh provides forecasts out to 15 days at both 25km and 3km resolution.

Description:
Weather data is everywhere. Decision-ready weather is not.

Every day, models, sensors, and observing networks generate enormous volumes of weather data — but most organizations still receive that information as raw files, imagery, or products that require interpretation before action can be taken. Most businesses do not need another weather map or another bulk data feed. They need operational answers they can act on immediately.

WxChange transforms weather data into decision-ready services. Built on a growing catalog of public and commercial weather datasets, the platform provides developer-friendly, operations-focused endpoints designed to deliver actionable answers instead of raw datasets alone — helping organizations integrate weather directly into planning, logistics, risk management, and day-to-day operations.

At the same time, WxChange serves as an open exchange for weather-data providers. Modeling teams, forecasters, and data producers can publish proprietary models, observations, and analytics through scalable, metered APIs without needing to build and maintain their own large-scale web infrastructure. WxChange handles the delivery layer, allowing producers to focus on the quality and value of their weather intelligence while making it instantly accessible through the same operational endpoints used by customers.

The result is a shared platform where weather producers and weather users operate on the same pipeline — connecting atmospheric data directly to operational decision-making.

Built by the team behind core elements of the U.S. Air Force Weather cloud data enterprise, WxChange brings mission-scale weather infrastructure and decision-ready weather services to the broader commercial ecosystem.

Stop by our booth in Denver to see where the exchange is headed.

Description:
Pitch Aeronautics brings localized, near-time weather conditions to the electric utility industry. We provide a vertically integrated stack of services and products including the Astria drone, WireWarrior weather sensor, and WireWeather software.

The Astria drone platform allows us to install WireWarrior sensors directly onto energized power lines. Once installed our sensors capture real-time wind speed and temperature precisely where weather-driven risk is greatest.

The WireWeather platform synthesizes the field-based weather observations with national physics-based models to produce statistical short-term wind and temperature forecasts. By grounding broad atmospheric models in actual microclimatic conditions along the line, WireWeather delivers hyperlocal weather data directly to the utilities. Machine learning models continuously refine these forecasts by learning from unique terrain effects, microclimates, and historical patterns along each span. This statistically refined data is displayed in a customizable, user-friendly interface to directly support fast, intelligent, and safe operational decisions

At Pitch our mission is to provide the local weather intelligence to safely increase transmission capacity in the grid, identify emerging wildfire risk, and operate with greater confidence. Visit our booth to learn more.

Description:
Wicked Skies is an independent atmospheric observation and data collection platform focused on building real-world environmental datasets for AI training, computer vision, forecasting, and geospatial analysis.

The platform continuously captures synchronized 4K sky, weather, and atmospheric conditions across multiple fixed-position camera systems. This creates a continuously expanding archive of real-world observational data designed for machine learning, environmental modeling, remote sensing validation, and atmospheric intelligence applications.

Unlike mobile or event-based weather footage, Wicked Skies operates as a persistent fixed-location observation network, allowing for repeatable long-duration environmental monitoring across changing lighting conditions, cloud structures, storm development, precipitation events, atmospheric transitions, and seasonal variation.

Each sequence is paired with structured ground-truth metadata and observational context, supporting AI and computer vision systems focused on: • Atmospheric analysis • Weather forecasting and modeling • Environmental pattern recognition • Geospatial and satellite validation • Remote sensing applications • Temporal scene understanding • Real-world computer vision training

Description:
Black Swift Technologies (BST) delivers unmatched aerial data through purpose-built, rugged Unmanned Aircraft Systems (UAS) designed to operate in the harshest environments on Earth. Whether dropping an aircraft into the eye of a Category 5 hurricane, flying into corrosive volcanic plumes, or providing critical tactical intelligence in heavy precipitation, our platforms execute missions where standard drones fail.

Every Black Swift aircraft is powered by our proprietary SwiftCore™ Flight Management System, a highly advanced, vertically integrated architecture providing a true "launch-and-forget" experience. BST remains at the forefront of providing scalable, AI-enabled navigation and autonomous aerial solutions for defense, scientific research, and industrial applications.

We are excited to have the capacity to display our platforms such as:

Black Swift S3™ UAS Our most advanced Vertical Takeoff and Landing (VTOL) powerhouse is built to transport heavy, swappable payloads (up to 6 lbs) through thin air, extreme cold, and heavy turbulence. Featuring a 20,000 ft MSL flight ceiling and double the loiter time of industry standards, the S3 is purpose-built for persistent remote monitoring, mountainous terrain rescue, and defense intelligence in tight spaces or jagged terrain.

Black Swift S0™ VTOL UAS Weighing under 6 lbs with a 15,000 ft flight ceiling, this lightweight, highly portable drone is uniquely capable of fully autonomous flights in extreme atmospheric conditions. It provides critical 3-D wind, pressure, temperature, and humidity profiling, making it ideal for tactical military operations, rapid emergency response, and localized weather forecasting where runway access is impossible.

Black Swift S0™ Air Deployed UAS Competitively selected by NOAA and the USAF, this expendable system is tube-launched directly from crewed aircraft (like the WP-3D Orion or C-130). It holds world records for UAS operations in severe conditions—including measuring winds of 191 knots and enduring 119 minutes inside a tropical storm. It features a flush-air sensing nosecone, a 1.8" field-swappable payload, and is currently pioneering multi-UAS cooperative swarming for extreme weather and military missions.

Description:
Our Mission

The Cooperative Institute for Research in the Atmosphere (CIRA) serves as a nexus for multi-disciplinary cooperation between NOAA research scientists and Colorado State University research staff, faculty, and students, aligning NOAA-identified research theme areas with long-standing academic strengths of the University.

Our mission is: to foster additional collaboration with national and international agencies who are developing related capabilities; to affect the fundamental research conducted at the University towards NOAA’s operational needs; and to communicate our research and its practical implications to the scientific community and the public.

To this end, we are dedicated to providing high-quality training to ensure operational user proficiency; conducting outreach programs to K-12 education and the general public to promote environmental literacy; and to quantifying and communicating the significant positive societal impacts of NOAA research on our everyday lives.

Description:
The mission of the U.S. National Science Foundation National Solar Observatory (NSF NSO) is to advance knowledge of the Sun, both as an astronomical object and as the dominant external influence on Earth, by providing forefront observational opportunities to the research community.

NSO built and operates the world’s most extensive collection of ground-based optical and infrared solar telescopes and auxiliary instrumentation— including the NSF-NOAA GONG network of six stations around the world, and the world’s largest solar telescope, the NSF Daniel K. Inouye Solar Telescope—allowing solar physicists to probe all aspects of the Sun, from the deep solar interior to the photosphere, chromosphere, the outer corona, and out into the interplanetary medium. These assets also provide data for heliospheric modeling, space weather forecasting, and stellar astrophysics research, putting our Sun in the context of other stars and their environments.

Besides the operation of cutting-edge facilities, the mission includes the continued development of advanced instrumentation both in-house and through partnerships, conducting solar research, and educational and public outreach. NSO is managed by the Association of Universities for Research in Astronomy, Inc. (AURA) under a cooperative agreement with NSF. For more information, visit nso.edu.

Description:
Forecast Verification and Market Intelligence for Weather Forecast Producers

ForecastWatch is the independent benchmark authority for forecast accuracy verification. Since 2003, we have built and maintained the world's largest proprietary database of forecast performance data - over a billion verified forecasts across thousands of global locations.

Our platform delivers three core capabilities:

1. Verification Platform - Producers upload forecasts; we measure accuracy using published methodology and return actionable diagnostics. No proprietary methods. No black boxes. Methodology available at forecastwatch.com/methodology.

2. Market Intelligence - The Most Accurate Forecast Awards (MAFA) program benchmarks forecast producers head-to-head across global regions and meteorological categories. Categories include temperature, precipitation, wind, and specialized forecasts (solar irradiance, aviation, severe weather). Winners earn credible third-party validation recognized throughout the industry.

3. Competitive Diagnostics - Producers see how their accuracy compares to peers on specific metrics and geographies, without disclosure of competitor identities. This channel-friendly approach lets producers improve without channel conflict.

Four Markets, One Benchmark:

  • Forecast Producers seeking competitive validation and actionable diagnostics
  • Grid Operators & Utilities verifying forecast quality for operational decisions
  • Energy Traders & Renewables Firms benchmarking solar and wind data providers
  • Airlines, Shipping & Logistics evaluating forecast performance for operational planning

2026 Award Winners: Microsoft, Foreca, DTN, Wettermanufaktur, Visual Crossing, Open-Meteo, OpenWeather, Atmospheric G2, CFAN, Google.

Launching 2027 MAFA Program: Join us at the booth to see this year's categories, expanded metrics, and new producer participants.

Description:
The Cooperative Institute for Severe and High-Impact Weather Research and Operations (CIWRO) is the largest research center at the University of Oklahoma, employing more than 215 researchers, support personnel and students. CIWRO was established in 2021 and extends cooperative programs between the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) and OU that have existed continually since 1978. CIWRO connects the scientific and technical resources of OU and NOAA with the goal of improving the basic understanding of weather and transitioning that understanding to operations to produce better forecasts that save lives and property.

Visit our booth to find out about our research opportunities for undergraduates and graduate students, postdoctoral fellowships, and full-time employment opportunities. We are happy to discuss all of the exciting research opportunities and connections that CIWRO can offer.

Description:
The School of Earth, Environmental, and Marine Sciences (SEEMS) at The University of Texas Rio Grande Valley (UTRGV) provides students with a unique integrative education and training experience that prepares them to meet the challenges and opportunities in the multiple dimensions of contemporary earth, environmental, and marine sciences.

UTRGV is a multi-campus distributed institution spanning the Rio Grande Valley in South Texas with two main core campuses in Brownsville, and Edinburg, alongside several specialty teaching and research locations across Harlingen, Weslaco, Port Isabel, and South Padre Islands.

The Master’s degree in Agricultural, Environmental, and Sustainability Sciences (AESS) provides students with a unique, integrative education and training experience that prepares them to meet the challenges and opportunities in the multiple dimensions of contemporary agricultural, environmental and sustainability science disciplines.

The Master’s degree in Ocean, Coastal, and Earth Sciences (OCES) provides students with a unique integrative education and training experience that prepares them to meet the challenges and opportunities in the marine, coastal, and environmental science disciplines.

Description:
LSU’s Coastal Meteorology graduate program examines the dynamic connections among the atmosphere, oceans, and coastlines. Students gain hands-on experience in atmospheric modeling, satellite and remote sensing, and drone-based field research while tackling critical challenges such as hurricanes, flooding, drought, erosion, air pollution, extreme heat, and land loss.

Graduates are prepared to turn science into solutions that protect lives, strengthen communities, and build a more resilient future. Career opportunities span the National Weather Service, NOAA, government agencies, research institutions, and private industry.

This graduate program complements LSU’s Coastal Meteorology undergraduate program, the only program of its kind in the nation. Both are housed in the Department of Oceanography & Coastal Sciences within the LSU College of the Coast & Environment.

Visit the LSU booth to discover where a degree in Coastal Meteorology can take you.

Description: The University of Utah Department of Atmospheric Sciences is the leading program of weather and climate related research and education in the Intermountain West and is recognized internationally for its expertise in cloud-climate interactions, mountain meteorology, climate physics and dynamics, weather and climate modeling, and tropical meteorology. Our research and teaching endeavors provide the knowledge and tools needed by society to address the challenges posed by hazardous weather and climate change in the 21st century. We are a student-centered department with faculty who are dedicated graduate student mentors and classroom instructors. Several of our professors have won college or university-wide teaching awards. We offer a minor, B.S., M.S., and Ph.D. in Atmospheric Sciences as well as the Research Experiences in Alpine Meteorology (REALM) REU program.

Description:
Observe. Measure. Understand: Uncrewed Systems and Tornado Science from CU Boulder MUSAS and Disaster Imaging Inc.

Visit the joint booth of the University of Colorado Boulder's Mobile Uncrewed Systems for Atmospheric Science (MUSAS) facility and Disaster Imaging Inc. (DII). We're partnering to expand what uncrewed aircraft systems (UAS) can do for atmospheric science, from routine boundary layer profiling to rapid response after violent tornadoes. Stop by to see our aircraft up close, explore recent datasets, and talk with our scientists, engineers, and pilots about bringing these capabilities to your research, classroom, or operations.

MUSAS: UAS for the Atmospheric Science Community

MUSAS is a National Science Foundation–sponsored Community Instruments and Facilities program. It gives researchers and educators access to a versatile fleet of uncrewed aircraft, instruments, and mobile field infrastructure, along with the experienced crews and airspace approvals needed to fly them. Our platforms have flown in the Great Plains, the Arctic, coastal regions, and over the open ocean.

  • RAAVEN: our primary fixed-wing aircraft, with flights of up to 2.5 hours and ranges over 100 km. It measures pressure, temperature, humidity, and three-dimensional winds, with optional aerosol, radiation, and high-frequency turbulence payloads.
  • Super RAAVEN: an extended-payload variant that carries cloud droplet probes, optical particle spectrometers, and aerosol sensors for aerosol-cloud and microphysics studies.
  • Mobile ground support: instrumented tracker vehicles for storm-relative operations, and the Mobile UAS Research Collaboratory, a field operations van with real-time computing, workstations for up to six aircraft, and a 50-foot meteorological mast.

Researchers and educators can request MUSAS through NSF's Facility and Instrumentation Request Process for education and outreach, single-facility research, or major field campaigns. Ask us how to get started.

Disaster Imaging Inc.: Understanding Tornadoes Holistically

DII is a women-owned nonprofit scientific organization working to understand tornadoes as complete systems, from the winds within the vortex to the damage left on the ground. Led by Erik N. Rasmussen, an architect of VORTEX, VORTEX2, VORTEX-SE, and PERiLS, DII combines three approaches:

  • Impact observations: rapid-response UAS surveys that document tornado damage at about 3 cm resolution, integrated with satellite, radar, and ground observations. These have revealed features such as cycloidal marks and the effects of terrain and land cover on tornado intensity.
  • Machine learning: AI tools that extract patterns from large damage datasets to characterize and predict tornado damage, intensity, and impacts.
  • High-resolution numerical simulations: models that resolve near-ground tornado winds and debris, down to individual debris trajectories.

DII shares its results with the National Weather Service and FEMA to strengthen warnings, damage assessments, and recovery, with special attention to rural communities that research has long overlooked. We are always looking for new collaborators. If you share our goal of advancing tornado science, let's talk.

Whether you study boundary layers, severe storms, aerosols, or hazard impacts, or you want to train the next generation of field scientists, come see how MUSAS and DII can help you observe the atmosphere in new ways.

Description:
Sparv Embedded develops lightweight, portable systems for high-quality atmospheric measurements in the field.

Windsond S2 is an ultra-light radiosonde, weighing under 9 grams, that provides real-time profiles of wind, temperature, humidity and pressure. Its compact design cuts helium consumption and simplifies logistics, so a single person can launch a full profile within minutes. Reusable configurations with controlled cut-down and GPS-based recovery allow repeated launches and dense, cost-effective profiling during field campaigns.

Sparvio is our modular sensor platform for UAV-based atmospheric measurements. It supports parameters such as temperature, humidity, wind, gases and particles.

Our systems are used by universities, research institutes, wildfire and emergency response teams, and defense users. What they have in common is a need for instruments that deploy quickly in places where conventional observing systems are impractical.

Based in Linköping, Sweden, Sparv Embedded combines expertise in electronics, sensors and software. We deliver complete measurement systems as well as customized solutions for atmospheric research and operational applications.

Visit us at AMS 2027 to see Windsond S2 and Sparvio up close and discuss how lightweight measurement systems can support your next field campaign.

Whether the question is a hurricane track, a hailstorm, or the hazard profile at a single address, the answer is grounded in a consistent, verifiable record.

To make these capabilities more broadly accessible to the weather enterprise, Athenium developed barocline, an AI-native platform for Earth intelligence. Through the Model Context Protocol, AI agents query that record directly, covering post-event forensics, asset-level conditions, interactive mapping, and more. Anyone, from insurance carriers to weather enthusiasts, can ask questions in plain language. Answers are sourced and logged with a full audit trail so every result can be traced, reviewed, and defended.

Description:
Skyfora transforms existing GNSS receivers on telecom cell towers into a dense, real-time atmospheric observation network—with software alone.

By measuring the delay of satellite signals travelling through the atmosphere, Skyfora delivers high-resolution water-vapour observations in real-time. These data give weather forecasters and AI model developers unique insight into the moisture conditions that drive rainfall and severe weather.

Built on infrastructure already deployed worldwide, Skyfora offers a scalable way to expand observation coverage in under-observed regions and add greater detail and more frequent updates in well-monitored areas.

More observations. Deeper atmospheric insight. New possibilities for forecasting and early warning.

Weather & Climate Intelligence 

All-weather intelligence with global, 24/7 coverage 

Spire provides space-based atmospheric observation and AI-driven forecasting that power accurate weather insight for industry and government. Its satellite constellation collects global GNSS Radio Occultation (RO) atmospheric profiles — including over remote regions and open oceans — measuring temperature, pressure, and humidity thousands of times per day. Spire also captures environmental indicators via GNSS-Reflectometry, including soil moisture, ocean winds, and sea ice, to support climate monitoring and disaster preparedness.  

These differentiated datasets power high-resolution forecasts over the continental U.S., Europe, and Southeast Asia and enable global AI-driven forecasts up to 46 days into the future, delivered via APIs and visualization dashboards. 

Commercial customers in energy, commodity trading, utilities, agriculture, and aviation use Spire’s weather intelligence to improve forecast skill where ground sensors are sparse, strengthen trading and operational decisions, optimize grid planning and renewable performance, and increase lead time for disruptive weather events. 

Spire’s RO, soil moisture, and ocean wind data are also ingested by NOAA and EUMETSAT to improve short-, medium-, and long-range forecasts and support mission-critical severe weather prediction.

Description:
Exhibit Description

2027 AMS Annual Meeting (107th) — 10–14 January 2027 — Denver, Colorado

Company Name: FP2FIRE, INC

Exhibit Title: Hydrogen Weather Balloon Safety

Hydrogen is the practical lift gas for today's upper-air program: it delivers about 13 percent more lift per cubic foot than helium, costs far less, and is not subject to the shortages and price volatility of a finite global helium supply. The National Weather Service has inflated sounding balloons with hydrogen since the 1960s. Yet hydrogen is a flammable gas. The International Fire Code prohibits using it to inflate balloons unless an approved equivalency demonstrates equivalent safety, and the 2026 edition of NFPA 2, Hydrogen Technologies Code, permits hydrogen-filled meteorological sounding balloons only where the inflation facility has been certified by a qualified engineer with expertise in hydrogen fire safety.

FP2FIRE, INC is that qualified engineer. Company President Martin T. Gresho, PE, chaired the NFPA 2 Hydrogen Technical Committee from 2005 through 2015, serves as a Principal member of the NFPA 55 and NFPA 400 committees, spent 15 years as Fire Marshal at Sandia National Laboratories' California site, serves currently as a Fire Marshal for the Coal Creek Canyon Fire Department in Colorado, and has designed and installed specialty hydrogen inflation systems at eight National Weather Service upper-air sites. FP2FIRE brings more than 40 years of fire protection engineering experience to every hydrogen project.

Drawing on this experience, FP2FIRE has developed and built the Hydrogen Inflation Safety System (HISS). Applying risk assessment methods from the chemical process industry, HISS monitors key parameters and controls automatic interlocks that stop the flow of hydrogen: a mass flow meter limits each fill to a preset batch volume, closing a normally closed outdoor solenoid valve at about 150 percent of the expected fill volume; a ventilation interlock allows no gas flow unless exhaust ventilation is running and keeps it running for 60 minutes after the fill; a timer automatically terminates abnormally long fills; and a manual reset readies the system for every fill event. HISS adds redundant belt-and-suspenders protection on top of typical buoyancy control systems. buoyancy fill valve.

The HISS is not a concept — it is built and has over 40 years of successful operating experience. Its design basis is documented in detailed site-specific engineering analysis as required by NFPA 2. The same turnkey engineering approach can be designed into new balloon inflation facilities or retrofitted into existing ones. FP2FIRE installs and services the HISS as well as hydrogen generation and storage these systems as well.

Visit our booth to see a HISS unit on display, review the underlying engineering analysis, and talk with our experts about making hydrogen a safe, economical lift gas for your upper-air program.
